title.narrative: Land for Life - Making Policies Work for Food Security, Phase III (ETH)

description.narrative: Contribution to improving food security through secure land rights in rural communities in Ethiopia

Land for Life Life Phase III supports the establishment and strengthening of multi-stakeholder partnerships (MAP) on land governance in Ethiopia. The aim is to bring together all relevant stakeholders such as civil society, government, private sector, academia or media, to build trust and collaborate for land-related policy and behavioral change. Especially rights holders and civil society are empowered to participate meaningfully in dialogue and partnerships. Phase III of the initiative builds on the achievements of phase I and II and focuses on the sustainability of the established multi-stakeholder processes and platforms.

There is a direct target group of in total 736 people:MAP actors, such as the Land for Life MAP secretariats, i.e. the staff of the partner organizations responsible for the implementation of the initiative, as well as the members of the MAP steering committees and thematic working groups (36 active members of the MAP committees).Other actors who are reached through MAP dialogues and activities (200 people):Civil Society Organizations (CBOs), farmers organizations, will be involved with the aim of increasing their participation in political decision-making and strengthening their collective power through increased collaboration.Academics and media representatives are involved with the aim of becoming more involved in change processes and advocacy through the sharing of knowledge and information.Representatives and decision-makers from government institutions and national and local authorities will be involved with the aim of opening up spaces for participation, partnering with civil society and other actors, and advocating for the implementation of responsible land policies that are in line with international standards.private investors and investment promotion agencies will be involved with the aim of applying the RAI principles and engaging more in dialogue with local communities and civil society.traditional leaders and customary institutions are involved with the aim of strengthening the inclusion of marginalized groups, ensuring the implementation of existing laws, and mobilizing communities.3. Approximately, more than 500 residents of rural communities will be strengthened and supported in their awareness of existing rights and in their possibilities to claim them. This is achieved through training, community-level dialogues.
